## Verdict

**Juno Board** costs least for a team of 15, at **$300 per month**. Its 25-seat minimum forces payment for 10 unused seats, but its low $12 rate still beats Heronry's $360 — where all 15 seats are billed at $24 — and Cygnus Flow's $850.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Juno Board | $12 | 25 |
| Cygnus Flow | $17 | 50 |
| Heronry | $24 | 5 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 15 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Juno Board:** minimum 25 > 15, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $12 = **$300 per month**. Effective rate $20.00 per person ($300 ÷ 15).
- **Cygnus Flow:** minimum 50 > 15, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $56.67 per person.
- **Heronry:** minimum 5 < 15, so 15 seats paid. 15 × $24 = **$360 per month**. Effective rate $24.00 per person.

Juno Board is $60 per month cheaper than Heronry ($720 per year) and $550 per month cheaper than Cygnus Flow ($6,600 per year).

## Risks

The margin over Heronry is thin — $60 per month — and it is created entirely by Juno Board's minimum, not by the rate. If the team shrinks, Juno Board's bill stays fixed at $300 while Heronry's falls with headcount; below 13 people Heronry becomes cheaper. Confirm expected headcount before committing.

Growth favours Juno Board. Past 25 seats its unused-seat penalty disappears and it scales at $12 against Heronry's $24.

This compares list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits or security, so the cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, discounts, onboarding fees and contract exit terms are not in the source and could reorder the ranking. Check whether the 25-seat minimum is enforced at signup or only at renewal.
